text:
jean: quick thought — we need a cleaner negotiation between canary controller and router for scaling and fallback. current ad-hoc handoffs are causing oscillation
samir: agree. seen spikes when canary expands then gets drained immediately. lose warm caches and increase p99s :grimace:
olga: can you sketch the problem? is it timing, weight smoothing, or lease contention?
jean: combo. controllers request extra capacity, router starts sending traffic, probe failures cause immediate rollback, controller then removes capacity. we should have a short 'grace credit' window so capacity isn't removed instantly.
matt: love the "grace credit" idea. basically give an allocation a budgeted period to prove health before eviction. prevents flip-flop.
samir: +1. also add a negotiated backpressure token so routers know capacity is provisional. routers treat provisional capacity with conservative split (eg 5% max) until confirmed.
olga: proposal sketch: 1) controller asks for N slots with lease TTL 60s; 2) router marks them as provisional and caps split to min(5%, configured); 3) if probes succeed for M seconds, controller promotes lease -> full split; 4) if fail, controller keeps the slot but marks degraded and returns to pool after TTL.
jean: exactly. we should emit signals for metrics: lease_state, provisional_weight, promote_latency. ops needs those for runbooks.
matt: can we encode config as small YAML? quick draft:

```yaml
canary_policy:
  provisional_ttl: 60  # seconds
  provisional_max_pct: 5
  promotion_window: 20  # seconds of successful probes
  backoff_on_fail: 30   # seconds before retry
```

samir: that looks good. one more: per-tenant fairness. provisional slots shouldn't starve regular traffic on multi-tenant hosts. router needs a tenant_priority knob.
olga: important: split determinism. do we do probabilistic split or deterministic hashing while provisional? probabilistic is easier to cap but causes sampling variance. hashing keeps session affinity but may overload a single instance.
jean: prefer hybrid: deterministic when full split, probabilistic when provisional. explanation: provisional traffic is low volume, so randomness reduces hot spots. once promoted, we switch to hashed affinity for session consistency.
matt: edge case: what if promotion happens during an ongoing long session? we may break affinity. need migration hint in response headers so clients can rebind.
samir: implement header `X-Redwood-Canary-Hint: promoted` and a short-lived cookie for affinity migration. document in runbook.
infra-bot: deploy queued: canary-controller v2 -> staging (build 231). ETA 4m
jean: thanks infra-bot. next: fallback semantics. when router detects degraded probes it should route to fallback model variant but keep controller informed so it can start a graceful scale-down. controllers should prefer draining by new-session-only first.
olga: +1. prefer soft-drain: mark instance as `drain-new` then `drain-all` after a grace period. avoids killing in-flight requests.
matt: also add hysteresis for multi-region fallbacks — avoid global rollback loops if a single region blips. controller policy should require N region confirmations before global fallback.
samir: can we add a small state diagram in the docs? quick ASCII:

```
REQUEST -> router decides: provisional?promotional?full
provisional -> limited traffic -> probes -> promoted OR revert
promoted -> full traffic -> normal health checks
revert -> soft-drain -> release capacity
```

jean: nice. action items: Samir to PR router split & header, Matt to update controller lease API + promotion TTL, Olga to add metrics and runbook changes. I'll write the architecture follow-up RFC with these pieces.
samir: ping me when RFC draft is up — want to ensure rollout-safe defaults.
matt: I'll include a canary test harness to simulate probe flaps so we can tune provisional_max_pct and promotion_window.
jean: cool. if nobody objects I'll capture this and open a thread in eng-runtime for implementation sync. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment started: canary-controller v2 -> staging (build 231)
jean: thanks all. saved a link to the runbook draft in #docs once it's ready.
